questions.question: Choose the sentence where the underlined word does NOT function as an interjection but as a different part of speech.

options.text: "Indeed, that was a remarkable effort from the entire team."
"Well, I suppose we could try a different approach."
"The well in the village had provided water for over a century."
"Oops! I did not mean to send that message to everyone."

questions.question:
In the following sentence, what type of interjection is used?
"Hooray! We have finally been selected for the national competition!"

options.text: Cognitive
Volitive
Emotive
Agreement

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary interjection?

options.text: Well
Sure
Indeed
Ouch

questions.question:
Select the interjection in the following sentence:
"Oh well, there is nothing more any of us can do about the situation now."

options.text: situation
nothing
Oh well
more

questions.question:
Identify the misplaced modifier in the following sentence:
"She nearly drove for four hours without stopping for a break."

options.text: nearly
without stopping
for a break
for four hours

questions.question:
Pick the option that best explains why the following sentence contains a dangling modifier:
"After finishing the assignment, the television was switched on immediately."

options.text: The modifier is placed too far from the verb it is meant to describe.
The sentence lacks a logical subject who is finishing the assignment.
The verb is in the wrong tense for the modifier to work correctly.
The modifier is a prepositional phrase rather than a participial phrase.

questions.question:
Which of the following is the most effective revision of this sentence to avoid a dangling modifier?
"Hoping to catch the early bus, the alarm was set for five in the morning."

options.text: Hoping to catch the early bus, the alarm was set at five in the morning.
The alarm was set for five in the morning, hoping to catch the early bus.
Hoping to catch the early bus, she set the alarm for five in the morning.
Set for five in the morning, the early bus was what she hoped to catch.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a clause modifier?

options.text: broad
trembling
of medium height
although he was exhausted

questions.question: A student is asked to sort four sentences by voice. Three are in active voice. One is not. Which is the odd one out?

options.text: The chef prepared a three-course meal for the visiting delegates.
The architect designed the bridge to withstand heavy coastal winds.
The farewell dinner was organised by the students for their teacher.
The journalist published the article before the evening deadline.

questions.question:
A teacher writes this sentence on the board:
"The trophies were arranged on the display shelf before the ceremony began."
She then tells her students to convert it to active voice.
Zoe writes: "Someone arranged the trophies on the display shelf before the ceremony began."
Ben writes: "The trophies arranged on the display shelf before the ceremony began."
Which student got it right?

options.text: Only Zoe
Only Ben
Both Zoe and Ben
Neither Zoe nor Ben

questions.question: A teacher puts four sentences on the board and tells the class that one contains an error in its passive voice structure. Which one is it?

options.text: The old photographs had been stored in a box beneath the stairs for decades.
The farewell speech will be delivered by the outgoing head of department tomorrow.
The injured passenger was took to the nearest hospital by the paramedics.
The school gates are locked every evening at half past five.

questions.question:
A teacher writes this sentence on the board:
"Someone left the gate open."
She then asks the students to transform it using passive voice.
Two students attempt the conversion:
Aisha writes: "The gate was left open."
Omar writes: "The gate was left open by someone."
Which student is correct?

options.text: Only Aisha
Only Omar
Both are correct
Neither Aisha nor Omar

questions.question: A student is checking her work. Her teacher asks her to find the sentence that is incorrectly punctuated.

options.text: "I haven't seen him since last Tuesday," she said slowly.
"Did you manage to finish the report on time?" he asked.
She whispered, "don't say a word to anyone about this."
"We should probably leave before it gets any later," he suggested.

questions.question:
A teacher writes this sentence on the board:
"She said that she was learning to play the piano."
She asks the class to convert it back into direct speech. Which option is correct?

options.text: She said, "I was learning to play the piano."
She said, "She is learning to play the piano."
She said, "I am learning to play the piano."
She said, "I had been learning to play the piano."

questions.question:
A teacher writes this sentence on the board:
"I enjoy reading," says Tariq.
She asks the class to convert it into indirect speech. Which option is correct?

options.text: Tariq said that he enjoyed reading.
Tariq says that he enjoys reading.
Tariq says that he enjoyed reading.
Tariq said that he enjoys reading.

questions.question:
A student is writing a story in which one character casually mentions a routine update to another.
Which sentence correctly applies the rule for using direct and indirect speech in dialogue?

options.text: "The meeting has been moved to Thursday afternoon," she told him.
She mentioned that the meeting had been moved to Thursday afternoon.
The meeting. Thursday. She told him just like that.
She told him by saying that the meeting has been rescheduled.

questions.question:
A teacher asks two students to write a sentence about the city of London.
Rahul writes: "London is the capital city of England and has a population of approximately nine million people."
Sophia writes: "London is by far the most exciting city in Europe and every visitor leaves thoroughly impressed."
Who wrote a fact?

options.text: Only Rahul wrote a fact.
Only Sophia wrote a fact.
Both Rahul and Sophia wrote facts.
Neither Rahul nor Sophia wrote a fact.

questions.question:
A teacher asks two students to write a sentence about climate change.
James writes: "According to NASA, global average temperatures have risen by approximately 1.1 degrees Celsius since the late nineteenth century."
Lena writes: "Anyone who denies climate change is simply being irresponsible and has no right to shape public policy."
Who wrote a fact?

options.text: Only James wrote a fact.
Only Lena wrote a fact.
Both James and Lena wrote facts.
Neither James nor Lena wrote a fact.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences contains a signal word or phrase that marks it as an opinion rather than a fact?

options.text: "The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert on Earth, covering approximately nine million square kilometres."
"In 1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest."
"In my view, electric vehicles are the only practical solution to reducing urban air pollution."
"The human body contains approximately two hundred and six bones in total."

questions.question:
A teacher writes the following sentence on the board:
"The cheetah can reach speeds of up to 112 kilometres per hour, making it the fastest land animal on Earth."
She then asks why this is a fact and not an opinion.

options.text: Because it uses formal, scientific language that sounds authoritative and reliable
Because most people already know and believe that cheetahs are fast, making it a widely accepted truth
Because it contains a specific, measurable claim about speed and a verifiable superlative that can be confirmed through scientific observation
Because the sentence does not contain any evaluative words such as "beautiful" or "impressive"
